shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: Analytical fields, navigation, and ghost actions. Cards keep only an inset top highlight.

shadows.name: pill-drop
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary-active) 45%, #000), 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 40%), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 45%, transparent)

shadows.name: card-highlight
shadows.purpose: Cards, Overview widgets, and metric tiles; paired with a sheen fading to the card surface within 64px.

shadows.name: elevation-control
shadows.purpose: Only for elements that borrow button classes without the Button slot, such as calendar navigation; Button pills use pill-drop.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Background, text, and border-color changes and tone-density swaps; no control translation.

motion.name: dither-field
motion.value: 12fps timer drift for 6s after arrival and while hovered; 600ms fade-in once drawn
motion.purpose: The sidebar identity field, the one ambient motion. Holds a still frame otherwise, pauses in background tabs, and never animates under reduced motion.

motion.name: menu-open
motion.value: 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) fade + scale from 0.96 at the trigger origin; 120ms fade for selects aligned over their trigger; 100ms fade out
motion.purpose: Menus, select popups, and popovers. Exits are faster than entries. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: overlay
motion.purpose: Dialog transition duration. Exit animations hold their last frame (animation-fill-mode: forwards) until unmount.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; transition: none; scroll-behavior: auto (elements and their ::before/::after)

loading.refresh: Retain current data; placeholders only for incoming regions.

focus.purpose: One visible keyboard outline across shared controls; no duplicated shadow ring.

narrative.overview:
Piko is a compact measurement tool using the user-selected Kanagawa palette. Sumi-ink surfaces and warm Fuji text frame Surimi Orange actions, Carp Yellow measurements, violet/aqua source categories, and green outcomes. Self-hosted Geist with Geist Pixel measurements, glossy pill controls, inset fields, single-frame segmented choices, ordered-dither screen tones, and the upright three-bar mark give the interface a precise character with a printed, 1-bit texture. Accessible shadcn Base UI primitives and Hugeicons provide the shared component language.

Analytical regions use flat surfaces, fine seams, aligned labels, and tabular values. Overview presents small square metrics, one wide activity chart, and paired reports; Explore retains its open analytical field. Editing and inspection use contained surfaces where boundaries clarify the task. Density serves reading: supporting context remains visible, and loading states preserve the geometry of the result they will replace. One palette is present in server-rendered HTML and CSS. There is no appearance selector, theme preference, or system-theme listener.
keyCharacteristics: Sumi-ink surfaces, warm text, orange actions, and yellow/violet/aqua data accents.
Geist typography: Geist for interface text, Geist Mono for literal code and identifiers, and Geist Pixel for page titles and measurements.
Ordered-dither (Bayer 4×4, 2px pixel) screen tones wherever the interface would otherwise use a translucent tint.
Flat analytical fields, small square metrics, and rectangular reports; contained forms and inspection.
Glossy pill actions and segmented choices, inset fields, one focus outline, and stable geometry.

rules.name: The Measured Color Rule
rules.body: Orange marks actions and destination selection; yellow, violet, and aqua distinguish measurements; green and red label outcomes. Selected choices and keyboard focus use warm yellow within the same palette.

rules.name: The Value Alignment Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for measurements, percentages, durations, and times that readers compare across rows. Geist Pixel has proportional digits only, so it is reserved for single headline values; anything compared down a column stays in Geist with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Shared Ground Rule
rules.body: Keep analytical regions flat and aligned. Fine boundaries group related measurements; reserve gloss for actions and soft elevation for temporary overlays.

rules.name: The Screen Tone Rule
rules.body: Where the interface would use a translucent tint, it uses an ordered-dither tone at the matching density instead. Dither is the only texture: don't combine it with blur or grain. Behind text, a tone is drawn in an ink darker than the face beneath it, so labels keep at least 4.5:1 on every pixel; lighter inks stay at 25% or sparser. The one exception is the modal backdrop, which puts a sparse dot screen over a translucent dim so a full-screen pattern never flickers. Under forced colors, controls gain a system outline and selected segments and the active page use the system highlight.

dos: Do reuse semantic theme variables to preserve one consistent palette from the first server paint.
Do preserve the shared upright three-bar logo/favicon, Geist, and the Kanagawa sumi-ink/orange/yellow relationship.
Do align measurements and use fine dividers to connect analytical regions.
Do use inset fields, pill segmented choices, and semantic hover/pressed/selection states.
Do express tints, fills, and state density with the shared ordered-dither tones at 2px pixels, keeping data marks exact.
Do keep visible labels, one ring-colored focus outline, readable metadata, and touch-sized controls on narrow screens.
Do preserve chart and table geometry while data loads or refreshes.
Do use TanStack charts, actual event identity kinds, and truthful empty or error states.
Do keep Overview metric tiles square and analytical reports flat while preserving their exact measures, local loading, and responsive reading order.
donts: Don't return to a corporate blue card grid or a black neon terminal identity.
Don't wrap every measurement in a raised, rounded card.
Don't reintroduce split-arrow compartments, individual segment frames, or filled orange destination navigation. Gloss belongs to pill actions only.
Don't add decorative botanical imagery, faux paper textures, grain, blur, or ornamental glow; dither is the only texture.
Don't replace useful event context with decoration or hide an actual loading failure behind a skeleton.
Don't turn either the Explore composition or the Overview report composition into a mandatory layout for every page.
